content:
incident-bot: Pager — canary rollout R-2026-0317-07 (us-west-2, wave-7) triggered abort criteria: 5xx rate 4.5% over 2m, healthcheck failure rate 12%. Runbook: https://redwood/release-runbook/R-2026-0317-07 :rotating_light:
tina: Got it, paging thread. Who kicked off this rollout?
alex: I did the rollout — flipping rollout_v2_enable to 20% canary weight. Seeing the alerts now, rolling back.
sam: Logs show a pattern: KV cache eviction + OOM-like traces right before 503s. Sample:```2026-03-17T12:01:22Z model-serving[pid=321]: kv_cache: evict key=abc123 size=37MB; oom_try_alloc 268435456 -> failed; returning 503```
alex: Thanks. Initiating rollback for the canary group now: `/deploy rollback R-2026-0317-07 --scope canary`
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by alex. Rollback wave: canary only. Estimated completion ~45s.
maria: Customer impact: support dashboard shows ~12 distinct requests failed (frontend retries), mostly low-latency tier. No major customer pages yet but CS will monitor.
tina: @emma (cs-oncall) can you triage the queue and flag any customers who hit repeated failures? Also engage customer success if needed.
emma: On it, creating support ticket and adding impacted request ids. Will notify if customers demand escalation.
alex: Also toggling feature flag kill-switch to stop further rollout: `ldctl set rollout_v2_enable false --env prod --scope canary`
deploy-bot: Feature flag rollout_v2_enable set to false by alex.
sam: After flag toggle, workers scaled down and OOM traces stopped. Metrics show KV eviction rate dropping.
alex: Can we confirm 5xx rate trending down?
tina: Metrics panel: 5xx rate dropped to 0.6% in last 90s, healthcheck fail rate down to 1.1%. Link: https://grafana/redwood/d/R-2026-0317-07
incident-bot: Incident created: `canary-health-failure-R-2026-0317-07`. Severity: P2. Add post-incident tasks.
maria: CS update: created customer-impact sheet, logged 12 impacted requests, none with SLA breaches so far. Will follow up if customers respond.
alex: Initial root cause hypothesis: the new batching optimization in v2 changed memory allocation patterns causing KV cache pressure and transient OOMs -> 503s.
sam: Opened PR to revert batching tweak: https://git.redwood/model-serving/pull/4678 — also adding additional guardrails to detect kv_cache OOM in canary health probe.
tina: Handoff: alex to own postmortem and follow-ups. Tasks: revert PR, extended soak test (24h) in staging with load profile, add KV OOM to abort criteria, and add a circuit-breaker metric.
alex: Acknowledged. I'll post a timeline and preliminary postmortem by EOD.
maria: Thanks all. :white_check_mark: Please tag me in the postmortem when ready so CS can align customer comms.
tina: Closing coordinating loop here. If anything flares I'll re-open thread. Great work on fast rollback and flag kill-switch. :thumbsup:
